Gene Description

Skp1 (Cbf3d) is the small, essential adaptor protein of Saccharomyces cerevisiae that couples F-box proteins to larger assemblies. Its N-terminal BTB/POZ-like domain binds the N-terminal repeat of the cullin Cdc53 and its C-terminal helices clamp the ~40-residue F-box motif, so that in SCF (Skp1-Cdc53-F-box-Hrt1) ubiquitin ligases Skp1 holds an interchangeable substrate receptor (Cdc4, Grr1, Met30, Dia2, Mdm30, Das1, Saf1, Ufo1, Hrt3 and others) in register with the Hrt1-bound E2 Cdc34. Skp1 has no catalytic activity and does not itself recognise substrates; the receptor supplies specificity and the Cdc53-Hrt1 module supplies the ubiquitin-transfer chemistry. Through SCF(Cdc4) and SCF(Grr1) Skp1 is required for destruction of the Clb-Cdk inhibitor Sic1 and of the G1 cyclins at Start, and skp1 alleles arrest in G1 with stabilised Sic1; through other receptors it participates in Met4-dependent sulfur-amino-acid control, Fzo1 turnover during mitochondrial fusion, Mig2 and Gal80 degradation in galactose induction, Sir4 ubiquitylation at silent chromatin and Mrc1 turnover during S-phase checkpoint recovery. Skp1 binding to Cdc53 also displaces the Cand1-like inhibitor Lag2, which is a prerequisite for cullin rubylation (neddylation). Independently of ubiquitination, Skp1 is the fourth subunit of the CBF3 centromere-binding complex (Ndc10-Cep3-Ctf13-Skp1): it heterodimerises with the F-box/LRR protein Ctf13, and the Ctf13/Skp1 pair must be activated by the Sgt1-Hsp90 chaperone system before it can join Cep3 and Ndc10 on the CDEIII element to nucleate kinetochore assembly; skp1 alleles that disturb this cycle missegregate chromosomes, arrest in mitosis with short spindles and disorganise septins. Skp1 is also a stoichiometric subunit of the RAVE complex (Rav1-Rav2-Skp1) that promotes V-ATPase V1-V0 assembly, and forms a cullin-free complex with the F-box protein Rcy1 that supports recycling of the v-SNARE Snc1. The protein is distributed between nucleus and cytoplasm, with a centromere-bound CBF3 pool, and is highly conserved across eukaryotes (ortholog of human SKP1).

Reconstitution of G1 cyclin ubiquitination with complexes co... 		ACCEPT
Summary: Skp1 is required for the G1/S transition as the adaptor of SCF(Cdc4) and SCF(Grr1), the ligases that destroy the Clb-Cdk inhibitor Sic1 and the G1 cyclins; skp1 alleles arrest in G1 with unreplicated DNA and stabilised Sic1.
Reason: Core biological process. Skp1 does part of the work of the transition: it holds the receptor (Cdc4 or Grr1) on the Cdc53-Hrt1 core so that phosphorylated Sic1 or Cln1/2 can be ubiquitinated, and the reconstituted SCF(Cdc4) and SCF(Grr1) complexes require it. The same term is accepted for Cdc4 and Cdc53 in this repository and Skp1 is the yeast exemplar in the G1/S module. ComplexPortal row for SCF(Grr1): the cited reconstitution shows phosphorylated Cln1 is ubiquitinated by Skp1-Cdc53-Grr1 complexes with Rbx1 and Cdc34.

SKP1 connects cell cycle regulators to the ubiquitin proteol... 		KEEP AS NON CORE
Summary: Certain skp1 alleles (skp1-4, skp1-12) arrest as large-budded cells with 2C DNA and a short spindle; the block is genuine but mechanistically undefined (kinetochore/CBF3 failure with checkpoint arrest versus a Sic1-independent SCF requirement).
Reason: Kept as non-core, matching the grading of the same term on Cdc4 and Cdc53. The arrest is reproducible and is the phenotype that first linked Skp1 to the kinetochore, but a short-spindle, 2C arrest is a metaphase-like block rather than a demonstrated defect in the G2/M transition itself, and no substrate or CBF3 step has been assigned to it. The evidence supports a second role of Skp1 rather than its defining function. Bai et al. report that different skp1 alleles arrest in G1 or in G2.
Supporting Evidence:

Summary: skp1-3 and skp1-4, alleles that perturb the CBF3 assembly/turnover cycle through the Skp1-Sgt1 interaction, cause disorganised septins, random bud-scar patterns and cytokinesis failures.
Reason: Genuine mutant phenotype (full text cached) but a secondary, CBF3-dependent role: the authors propose that CBF3 acts as a passenger-like complex with Bir1 to coordinate segregation with cytokinesis, and only alleles affecting the CBF3 cycle, not outer-kinetochore mutants, affect septins. Skp1 contributes by assembling CBF3 rather than by organising septins itself, so the term is kept as a pleiotropic non-core process.

Summary: Skp1 (with Cdc53 and Dia2) co-precipitates ARS305 and ARS603 origin DNA in crosslinker-dependent ChIP, reflecting recruitment of SCF(Dia2) to origins.
Reason: The ChIP result is genuine (full text cached) but records the location of an SCF(Dia2) pool, not a binding activity of Skp1: Skp1 has no DNA-binding domain, the authors conclude that Dia2 is the origin-binding protein, and Skp1 reaches origins only as the F-box adaptor of that complex. A molecular-function annotation to origin DNA over-reads crosslinked co-precipitation; this matches the grading of the same row on Cdc53. A chromatin/origin location on the SCF(Dia2) complex would represent the finding better.

Summary: Saf1 is an F-box protein; the informative activity behind this interaction is Skp1 binding the F-box motif of Saf1, which is how Skp1 tethers the receptor to the Cdc53-Hrt1 core (or, for Ctf13, into CBF3).
Reason: The cited work supports a more informative molecular function than bare protein binding: F-box domain binding (GO:1990444). Skp1 binds F-box proteins through the ~40-residue F-box motif (Bai et al., PMID:8706131), and this is the defining contact of the adaptor. Seol et al. recovered Saf1 among the nine F-box proteins associated with Skp1 by sequential affinity purification and mass spectrometry; the interaction is through the F-box, as for every other receptor.
Proposed replacements: F-box domain binding

Summary: Cdc53 is the cullin scaffold of SCF; the informative activity behind this interaction is Skp1 binding the N-terminal cullin repeat of Cdc53, the second of the two contacts that define the adaptor.
Reason: The cited work supports the specific molecular function cullin family protein binding (GO:0097602), the term already carried by IBA and used for the human SKP1-CUL1 rows, rather than bare protein binding; because the cullin contact is one half of the bridge by which Skp1 joins the receptor to the Cdc53-Hrt1 core, the activity it enables is ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity (GO:0160072), the term used for human SKP1 in the SCF GO-CAM models. Seol et al. recovered Cdc53 and all SCF components in sequential Skp1/Cdc53 purifications.
Proposed replacements: cullin family protein binding ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity

Requirement of Skp1-Bub1 interaction for kinetochore-mediate... 		MODIFY
Summary: Bub1 associates with centromere DNA via Skp1, and a Skp1 mutant that cannot bind Bub1 fails to mount the mitotic delay triggered by kinetochore tension defects while retaining the nocodazole, kinetochore-assembly and Mps1-overexpression arrests.
Reason: Bare protein binding hides the functional claim of the paper, which is that the Skp1-Bub1 contact transmits the tension-defect signal into the spindle checkpoint. The better term is mitotic spindle assembly checkpoint signaling (GO:0007094), which the authors support with a separation-of-function Skp1 allele. This is a single, abstract-only study on a role separate from SCF and CBF3 assembly, so the replacement should be treated as non-core; SGD did not add a checkpoint process term from this paper, and the proposal is flagged in suggested_questions.
Proposed replacements: mitotic spindle assembly checkpoint signaling
Supporting Evidence:
PMID:12769845
The Skp1's interaction with Bub1 is required for the mitotic delay induced by kinetochore tension defects, but not for the arrest induced by spindle depolymerization, kinetochore assembly defects, or Mps1 overexpression.
PMID:12769845
We propose that the Skp1-Bub1 interaction is important for transmitting a signal to the spindle checkpoint pathway when insufficient tension is present at kinetochores.

Reason: The cited work supports a more informative molecular function than bare protein binding: F-box domain binding (GO:1990444). Skp1 binds F-box proteins through the ~40-residue F-box motif (Bai et al., PMID:8706131), and this is the defining contact of the adaptor. Kus et al. reconstituted and purified a defined SCF complex containing Rcy1 together with Skp1, Cdc53 and Hrt1, the assembly that depends on the F-box-Skp1 contact.
Proposed replacements: F-box domain binding

Summary: Cdc53 is the cullin scaffold of SCF; the informative activity behind this interaction is Skp1 binding the N-terminal cullin repeat of Cdc53, the second of the two contacts that define the adaptor.
Reason: The cited work supports the specific molecular function cullin family protein binding (GO:0097602), the term already carried by IBA and used for the human SKP1-CUL1 rows, rather than bare protein binding; because the cullin contact is one half of the bridge by which Skp1 joins the receptor to the Cdc53-Hrt1 core, the activity it enables is ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity (GO:0160072), the term used for human SKP1 in the SCF GO-CAM models. Skp1 and Cdc53 are the shared core of all thirteen reconstituted complexes.
Proposed replacements: cullin family protein binding ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity

Summary: Ctf13 is an F-box protein; the informative activity behind this interaction is Skp1 binding the F-box motif of Ctf13, which is how Skp1 tethers the receptor to the Cdc53-Hrt1 core (or, for Ctf13, into CBF3).
Reason: The cited work supports a more informative molecular function than bare protein binding: F-box domain binding (GO:1990444). Skp1 binds F-box proteins through the ~40-residue F-box motif (Bai et al., PMID:8706131), and this is the defining contact of the adaptor. Ctf13 is the F-box protein of CBF3; Skp1 binds it as a heterodimer (Russell et al., PMID:10352012) and here the in vitro binding assays and kinetochore-assembly protocol show Skp1p acts through Ctf13p.
Proposed replacements: F-box domain binding

Summary: Sgt1 binds Skp1 (through the Skp1 BTB/POZ region and the Sgt1 TPR domain), and the Skp1p-Sgt1p interaction is critical for CBF3 assembly; skp1-4 blocks and skp1-3 stabilises the interaction.
Reason: A functionally important interaction, but its content is captured by the kinetochore-assembly rows (GO:0051382) from the same paper, and no GO molecular-function term describes Skp1's side of the Skp1-Sgt1 contact (Sgt1 supplies the TPR domain; Skp1 is the ligand). Bare protein binding adds no functional information about Skp1, so the row is removed; removal does not mean the interaction is false, and the Sgt1-Hsp90 axis is discussed in the notes.

Summary: Cdc53 is the cullin scaffold of SCF; the informative activity behind this interaction is Skp1 binding the N-terminal cullin repeat of Cdc53, the second of the two contacts that define the adaptor.
Reason: The cited work supports the specific molecular function cullin family protein binding (GO:0097602), the term already carried by IBA and used for the human SKP1-CUL1 rows, rather than bare protein binding; because the cullin contact is one half of the bridge by which Skp1 joins the receptor to the Cdc53-Hrt1 core, the activity it enables is ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity (GO:0160072), the term used for human SKP1 in the SCF GO-CAM models. Full text cached: Cdc53 is in Skp1 immunoprecipitates, the skp1-12 L8G mutation abolishes Cdc53 binding, and Skp1 binding to Cdc53 is what evicts the Cand1-like inhibitor Lag2.
Proposed replacements: cullin family protein binding ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity

Skp1 forms multiple protein complexes, including RAVE, a reg... 		MODIFY
Summary: Skp1 is a subunit of the RAVE complex (Rav1-Rav2-Skp1), which binds cytosolic V1 sectors and promotes assembly of the V-ATPase holoenzyme; loss of RAVE gives the vma phenotype. Genetic interaction row with RAV1.
Reason: The term names the downstream outcome (proton pumping by the assembled V-ATPase) rather than the step RAVE performs. RAVE is an assembly factor: it associates with V1 released by glucose deprivation and is needed for stable V1-V0 assembly even in glucose-grown cells, so the process Skp1 participates in is V-ATPase complex assembly (GO:0070072), already annotated from Smardon et al. Proposing that term as the replacement keeps the evidence and drops the indirect claim. Skp1's own contribution inside RAVE remains undefined (its recruitment is constitutive and is not the assembly signal), so the RAVE function is graded non-core.
Proposed replacements: vacuolar proton-transporting V-type ATPase complex assembly

Summary: skp1-12 (an allele defective for Cdc53 binding) shows mitotic-exit and cytokinesis defects and a specific genetic interaction with bfa1-delta; Skp1 binds the C-terminal 184 residues of the MEN inhibitor Bfa1 without affecting Bfa1 turnover.
Reason: Single abstract-only study (J Microbiol 2006) proposing an SCF-independent role in mitotic exit; the phenotype and the Bfa1 interaction are reported directly, but no mechanism (Skp1 does not control Bfa1 abundance) and no independent confirmation exist, and skp1-12 also perturbs CBF3-dependent functions that could delay exit indirectly. Summary: Skp1 assembles the SCF ligases whose receptor-selected substrates (Sic1, Cln1/2, Met4, Far1, Cdc6, Gcn4, Fzo1, Mig2, Sir4, Mrc1) are ubiquitinated for proteasomal destruction.

Core Functions

Adaptor/scaffold of SCF (Skp1-Cdc53-F-box-Hrt1) ubiquitin ligases: the BTB/POZ-like N-terminus binds the cullin Cdc53 while the C-terminal helices bind the F-box motif of an interchangeable receptor (Cdc4, Grr1, Met30, Dia2, Mdm30, Das1, Saf1, Ufo1, Hrt3 and others), holding the receptor-bound phospho-substrate in register with the Hrt1-bound E2 Cdc34 so that Sic1, Cln1/2, Met4, Far1 and other targets are polyubiquitinated for proteasomal destruction; Sic1 and Cln removal drives the G1/S transition.

Molecular Function:
ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity
Directly Involved In:
SCF-dependent proteasomal ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolic process protein ubiquitination G1/S transition of mitotic cell cycle
Cellular Locations:
nucleus cytoplasm
In Complex:
SCF ubiquitin ligase complex

F-box-binding subunit of the CBF3 inner-kinetochore complex: Skp1 heterodimerises with the F-box/LRR protein Ctf13, and the Ctf13/Skp1 pair, once activated by the Sgt1-Hsp90 chaperone system, assembles with the Cep3 and Ndc10 dimers on centromeric CDEIII DNA to nucleate kinetochore formation; Skp1-Sgt1 binding contributes to the rate-limiting Ctf13-Ndc10 step and balances CBF3 assembly against Ctf13 turnover.

Molecular Function:
F-box domain binding
Directly Involved In:
kinetochore assembly
Cellular Locations:
kinetochore nucleus
In Complex:
CBF3 complex

Suggested Questions for Experts

Q: What is Skp1's molecular contribution inside the RAVE complex and the cullin-free Rcy1-Skp1 complex? Rav1 and Rcy1 bind Skp1 through F-box-like contacts, yet neither assembly contains Cdc53/Hrt1; does Skp1 act as a structural adaptor there, or does it recruit an alternative partner, and should these pools carry a molecular function distinct from ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity?

Q: Should the Skp1-Bub1 tension-checkpoint finding (PMID:12769845), now recorded only as protein binding, be represented as a mitotic spindle assembly checkpoint signaling annotation, and is it reproducible with the separation-of-function skp1 allele in a clean background given that SGD did not add a checkpoint term from the paper?

Q: Which of the receptor-specific downstream outputs attached to the shared adaptor (HXT induction, GAL1 derepression, mitochondrial fusion, Sir4-dependent silencing, checkpoint recovery, methylmercury resistance) should be modelled as SCF(F-box) complex-level GO-CAM activities with the F-box protein as the specificity subunit, leaving Skp1 with the scaffold activity and the SCF-dependent catabolic process?

Suggested Experiments

Experiment: Combine skp1-4 and skp1-12 with mad2-delta or bub1-delta and score spindle length, Pds1 stability and anaphase entry at the restrictive temperature; a checkpoint-dependent arrest would be bypassed (with missegregation), whereas an SCF-dependent block would persist. In parallel, test a Skp1 variant carrying the Ctf13-interface substitutions (Y139/N140) in an otherwise SCF-competent background.

Hypothesis: The G2/M (metaphase-like) arrest of skp1-4 and skp1-12 cells is caused by loss of CBF3-dependent kinetochore function and consequent spindle-checkpoint activation, not by a Sic1-independent SCF requirement.

Type: genetic epistasis with checkpoint mutants and interface alleles

Experiment: Express phospho-null and phospho-mimetic SKP1 alleles at the endogenous locus and quantify the F-box protein repertoire co-purifying with Skp1 by SILAC/MS across nutrient conditions, then measure Met4, Sic1 and Cln2 half-lives to link altered receptor loading to substrate turnover.

Hypothesis: Skp1 phosphorylation at S162 (and T177) tunes receptor selection in vivo by weakening particular F-box contacts.

Type: phosphosite mutagenesis with quantitative interactome proteomics

Functional annotation report: Saccharomyces cerevisiae SKP1 (UniProt P52286)

1. Identity verification

The requested target is the budding-yeast gene SKP1, also called CBF3D, ordered locus YDR328C, from Saccharomyces cerevisiae S288c. The literature identifies budding-yeast Skp1p as an approximately 29–32-kDa protein that is both a subunit of the CBF3 kinetochore complex and the conserved adaptor in Skp1–Cullin–F-box (SCF) ubiquitin ligases. This agrees with the supplied UniProt description and with assignment to the Skp1/Skp1-like and BTB/POZ-related structural families. (kitagawa1999sgt1encodesan pages 1-2, willhoft2017thecrystalstructure pages 2-3, galan2001skp1pandthe pages 10-11)

No contradictory yeast identity was found. Literature on human SKP1A, Caenorhabditis elegans SKR-1/SKR-2, Schizosaccharomyces pombe Skp1, or parasite Skp1 homologues concerns different proteins and was excluded from the functional annotation. The conclusions below therefore concern P52286/YDR328C unless explicitly identified as broader mechanistic context.

2. Executive functional annotation

Skp1 is an essential, nonenzymatic protein-interaction adaptor. It does not catalyze ubiquitin transfer, bind centromeric DNA sequence-specifically, or itself recognize most SCF substrates. Its primary molecular activity is to bind proteins carrying an F-box and incorporate them into functional assemblies. In canonical SCF ligases, Skp1 connects an F-box substrate receptor to the Cdc53/Cul1–Rbx1/Hrt1 catalytic scaffold. In the CBF3 kinetochore, it binds the F-box protein Ctf13 and contacts Cep3, stabilizing the centromere-recognition complex. It also participates in an apparently non-SCF complex with Rcy1 during endosomal recycling. (kitagawa1999sgt1encodesan pages 1-2, willhoft2017thecrystalstructure pages 1-2, leber2018structuralbasisfor pages 5-6, galan2001skp1pandthe pages 1-1)

Consequently, Skp1 has no enzyme reaction or intrinsic substrate specificity analogous to an enzyme or transporter. The relevant “substrate specificity” is delegated to its F-box partner: Cdc4 recognizes phosphorylated cell-cycle substrates such as Sic1; Grr1 regulates G1 cyclins; Met30 controls Met4/Met32 and sulfur-stress signaling; Ctf13 incorporates Skp1 into CBF3 rather than a canonical degradation complex. (kitagawa1999sgt1encodesan pages 1-2, harris2024molecularinsightsintoa pages 24-27, lauinger2024cadmiumbindingby pages 1-2)

Functional context / complex Skp1’s precise role Location Key direct evidence and quantitative result Evidence confidence
Canonical SCF ubiquitin ligases: Skp1–Cdc53/Cul1–Rbx1/Hrt1–F-box protein Noncatalytic adaptor, not the catalytic E3 center: binds Cdc53 and an interchangeable F-box receptor, thereby connecting substrate recognition to the RING/E2 ubiquitin-transfer machinery. SCF^Cdc4 targets phosphorylated Sic1; SCF^Grr1 regulates G1 cyclins; SCF^Met30 controls Met4/Met32 and sulfur metabolism. Nucleocytoplasmic, depending on the F-box receptor and substrate; cell-cycle substrates and Met4 regulation prominently involve the nucleus. Skp1 inactivation causes G1 and G2 arrest and impairs ubiquitin-dependent turnover of CDK regulators. Biochemistry identified Skp1 with Cdc53, F-box proteins, and Rbx1/Hrt1; Sgt1 co-fractionated with Skp1-containing ligase activity in an apparent 200 ± 50-kDa fraction. (kitagawa1999sgt1encodesan pages 1-2, harris2024molecularinsightsintoa pages 24-27, kitagawa1999sgt1encodesan pages 5-6) High—genetic, biochemical, and structural evidence; individual substrate specificity belongs to the F-box receptor, not Skp1 itself.
CBF3 inner-kinetochore complex Structural assembly adaptor: binds the F-box/LRR protein Ctf13 and also contacts Cep3, stabilizing the complex that recognizes centromeric CDEIII DNA. Skp1 does not itself provide the primary sequence-specific DNA-binding activity; Cep3 recognizes CDEIII. Nuclear centromeres / inner kinetochore. Full CBF3 has Ndc10₂:Cep3₂:Ctf13₁:Skp1₁ stoichiometry and is approximately 445 kDa; the approximately 220-kDa Cep3₂–Ctf13–Skp1 core was reconstructed by cryo-EM at 3.6 Å. Skp1 helices α6–α8 and residues 105–112 engage the Ctf13 F-box/LRR region; Y139/N140 mutations prevented complex formation. Skp1 is an assembly platform, not an Hsp90 ATPase or cochaperone catalyst. Cytosol and nucleus; functionally relevant to assembly of SCF complexes and nuclear CBF3. A 2.8-Å Sgt1^TPR–Skp1^BTB crystal structure defined the interface. Full-length Sgt1 and Sgt1 residues 1–150 bound Skp1 with Kd ≈ 0.6–0.7 μM; alteration of Skp1 residues 65–74 abolished a detectable ITC isotherm. About 2% of total Skp1 was associated with Sgt1 in yeast extracts. (willhoft2017thecrystalstructure pages 2-3, willhoft2017thecrystalstructure pages 6-7, willhoft2017thecrystalstructure pages 1-2, kitagawa1999sgt1encodesan pages 5-6) High—crystallography, ITC, solution biochemistry, co-immunoprecipitation, and yeast genetics.

This is not established as a canonical catalytic SCF E3. Endosomal/Golgi recycling pathway and polarized-growth regions; Rcy1 occurs in cytoplasmic patches at buds, bud necks, and shmoo tips. Predominantly nucleocytoplasmic SCF signaling controlling nuclear Met4/Met32 responses and cellular sulfur/glutathione homeostasis. Table: Direct evidence for the molecular roles and cellular contexts of S. cerevisiae S288c Skp1/P52286. The table distinguishes Skp1’s noncatalytic adaptor function from the activities of SCF catalytic components, F-box receptors, and stress-sensing domains.

3. Canonical function in SCF ubiquitin ligases

Architecture and mechanism

A canonical yeast SCF consists of Skp1, the cullin scaffold Cdc53, Rbx1/Hrt1, and an interchangeable F-box protein. Skp1 binds the F-box receptor and the cullin, positioning the receptor-bound substrate near the RING-associated E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme. Thus, the assembled complex is an E3 ubiquitin ligase, but Skp1 itself is a noncatalytic bridge rather than the catalytic ubiquitin-transfer subunit. (harris2024molecularinsightsintoa pages 24-27, willhoft2017thecrystalstructure pages 2-3)

Structurally, Skp1 has an N-terminal BTB/POZ-like region associated with cullin and Sgt1 interactions and a C-terminal helical region that embraces F-box motifs. The roughly 35-residue C-terminal extension involved in F-box binding and the overall Skp1–F-box interaction mode are conserved among eukaryotes. (willhoft2017thecrystalstructure pages 2-3)

Cell-cycle pathway

Direct yeast genetics established that Skp1 inactivation can arrest cells in both G1 and G2 and disrupt ubiquitin-dependent turnover of CDK regulators. SCF^Cdc4 ubiquitylates Sic1, an inhibitor of S-phase CDK activity; its degradation permits cell-cycle progression. SCF complexes using other receptors extend Skp1-dependent regulation to G1 cyclins and additional phosphorylated regulators. Temperature-sensitive skp1 mutants exhibit chromosome-missegregation and cell-cycle-arrest phenotypes, while all four CBF3 components—including Skp1—are essential for viability. (kitagawa1999sgt1encodesan pages 1-2, harris2024molecularinsightsintoa pages 24-27)

The strongest interpretation is therefore not that Skp1 is a pathway-specific enzyme, but that it is a reusable molecular coupling module. Mutating or depleting it simultaneously compromises multiple F-box assemblies, explaining its essentiality and pleiotropic cell-cycle phenotypes.

4. CBF3 and kinetochore assembly

Structural role

Budding yeast uses short “point centromeres.” CBF3 recognizes the CDEIII element and initiates assembly of the inner kinetochore, which in turn supports deposition and positioning of the centromeric Cse4 nucleosome. Skp1 forms a tight heterodimer with the F-box/leucine-rich-repeat protein Ctf13 and attaches that module to a Cep3 dimer. Cep3—not Skp1—provides the principal sequence-specific CDEIII recognition through its Gal4-type Zn₂Cys₆ DNA-binding domain. (leber2018structuralbasisfor pages 1-2, leber2018structuralbasisfor pages 5-6)

Cryo-EM and solution analysis support an intact CBF3 stoichiometry of Ndc10₂:Cep3₂:Ctf13₁:Skp1₁, with an estimated mass near 445 kDa. The resolved Cep3₂–Ctf13–Skp1 core is approximately 220 kDa and was reconstructed at 3.6 Å resolution. Steric exclusion prevents a second Ctf13–Skp1 heterodimer from occupying the symmetric Cep3 dimer, explaining the asymmetric 2:1:1 core stoichiometry. (leber2018structuralbasisfor pages 2-3, leber2018structuralbasisfor pages 1-2, leber2018structuralbasisfor pages 3-5)

Skp1’s C-terminal helices α6–α8 bind the Ctf13 F-box, while Skp1 residues 105–112 form an additional loop contacting both the Ctf13 F-box and leucine-rich repeats. Skp1 also contacts Cep3 and stabilizes one Cep3 Gal4 DNA-binding domain. Mutating Skp1 Y139 and N140 prevented complex formation in pull-down assays despite comparable protein expression, providing direct functional validation of the structural interface. (leber2018structuralbasisfor pages 2-3, leber2018structuralbasisfor pages 3-5, leber2018structuralbasisfor pages 5-6)

Functional interpretation

The Skp1–Ctf13 interaction is best viewed as an evolutionary reuse of the Skp1–F-box interface for kinetochore construction. In CBF3, Skp1’s primary role is structural and assembly-promoting rather than ubiquitin transfer. Biochemical reconstitution further showed that coexpression of Ctf13 with Skp1 restored CBF3 activity, whereas either protein with Sgt1 alone did not; Ctf13–Skp1 also rescued defective CBF3 activity in sgt1-3 extracts. (kitagawa1999sgt1encodesan pages 4-5)

5. Sgt1–Hsp90-dependent assembly axis

Sgt1 is a cochaperone-associated assembly factor connecting Hsp90 to both SCF-associated proteins and the kinetochore. A 2.8-Å crystal structure showed the concave surface of the Sgt1 TPR domain binding the Skp1 BTB/POZ region. Purified full-length Sgt1 and an isolated Sgt1 TPR construct, residues 1–150, each bound Skp1 with a dissociation constant of approximately 0.6–0.7 μM. Alteration of Skp1 residues 65–74 abolished a detectable ITC binding isotherm, and yeast genetics indicated that Sgt1–Skp1 binding is an essential Sgt1 function. (willhoft2017thecrystalstructure pages 2-3, willhoft2017thecrystalstructure pages 6-7, willhoft2017thecrystalstructure pages 1-2)

Only about 2% of total Skp1 was estimated to associate with Sgt1 in yeast extracts. Sgt1–Skp1-containing material migrated at an apparent 200 ± 50 kDa and overlapped SCF ubiquitin-ligase activity. This low steady-state fraction is consistent with Sgt1 acting transiently in assembly or quality control rather than as a stoichiometric component of every mature Skp1 complex. (kitagawa1999sgt1encodesan pages 5-6)

6. Noncanonical role in membrane-protein recycling

Skp1 also binds the F-box protein Rcy1 in a complex lacking detectable Cdc53 and Hrt1. Two-hybrid reporter activity was 1,818 ± 134 or 2,187 ± 156 Miller units, depending on fusion orientation; mutation of three conserved Rcy1 F-box residues reduced activity to 631 ± 73, and F-box deletion reduced it to 91 ± 12. Co-immunoprecipitation recovered approximately 32-kDa Skp1 with Rcy1 but not canonical cullin/RING components, supporting classification as a non-SCF complex. (galan2001skp1pandthe pages 9-10, galan2001skp1pandthe pages 10-11)

Functionally, the Rcy1–Skp1 assembly contributes to post-endocytic recycling of the exocytic v-SNARE Snc1. In skp1-12 cells, about 40% displayed clearly intracellular GFP-Snc1, and only 49% of GFP-Snc1 was hyperphosphorylated, compared with approximately 70% in wild-type or canonical SCF-mutant cells. Mutants in Cdc34, Cdc53, or Hrt1 did not reproduce the recycling defect, separating this activity from conventional SCF-dependent ubiquitylation. (galan2001skp1pandthe pages 4-5, galan2001skp1pandthe pages 5-7)

Rcy1 localizes to cytoplasmic patches enriched at buds, bud necks, and mating projections; its CAAX motif, polarized secretion, and an intact actin cytoskeleton are required for this localization. These data locate the Rcy1-associated Skp1 function to polarized endosomal/Golgi recycling sites, although they do not demonstrate that the entire cellular pool of Skp1 shares Rcy1’s visible localization. (galan2001skp1pandthe pages 2-3, galan2001skp1pandthe pages 10-11)

7. Cellular localization

Skp1 should be annotated as a nucleocytoplasmic, complex-dependent protein, rather than as a resident of one organelle.

  • Nucleus/centromere: its CBF3 function is executed at centromeric CDEIII DNA in the inner kinetochore. The structural and genetic evidence for this location is direct and strong. (leber2018structuralbasisfor pages 1-2, leber2018structuralbasisfor pages 5-6)
  • Nuclear and cytosolic SCF pools: different F-box receptors recruit Skp1 to substrates controlling the cell cycle, transcription, nutrient responses, and protein turnover. Localization is consequently receptor- and substrate-dependent rather than specified by an intrinsic membrane anchor. (harris2024molecularinsightsintoa pages 24-27, lauinger2024cadmiumbindingby pages 1-2)
  • Endosomal/polarized-growth pathway: the Rcy1-bound fraction acts in Snc1 recycling associated with polarized cytoplasmic trafficking structures. This assignment is based primarily on Rcy1 and cargo localization plus Skp1-dependent trafficking phenotypes. (galan2001skp1pandthe pages 2-3, galan2001skp1pandthe pages 10-11)

Skp1 is not a transporter, secreted protein, integral membrane protein, or sequence-specific DNA-binding protein.

8. Recent developments, 2023–2024

Cadmium sensing by SCF^Met30

The most important recent Skp1-relevant advance is a 2024 mechanistic study of SCF^Met30. Met30’s F-box cysteines C201, C205, and C211 bind cadmium with a reported K_D of approximately 8 μM. Cadmium induces a conformational change and Met30 autoubiquitylation, recruiting Shp1 and the Cdc48/p97 segregase. Cdc48 then extracts Met30 from the Cdc53–Skp1 core, disassembling SCF^Met30 and relieving ubiquitylation-dependent repression of Met4/Met32-controlled stress programs. (lauinger2024cadmiumbindingby pages 8-9, lauinger2024cadmiumbindingby pages 1-2, lauinger2024cadmiumbindingby pages 2-3)

This result refines the annotation of Skp1: the Skp1–F-box interface is not merely a static bridge but a regulated disassembly point. Nevertheless, Met30, not Skp1, is the demonstrated cadmium sensor. Inactivation of SCF^Met30 supports sulfur-metabolite restoration and glutathione production during cadmium stress. (lauinger2024cadmiumbindingby pages 1-2)

Hydrogen-sulfide and sulfur-flux sensing

A separate 2024 study found that hydrogen sulfide is sufficient to induce Met4 ubiquitylation in vivo and implicated cysteines in Met30’s WD40 region in sulfur sensing. Met30 contains 23 cysteines, nearly all of which remained reduced under the tested sulfur-replete and sulfur-deficient conditions. The proposed persulfidation or metal-dependent mechanisms therefore remain hypotheses rather than established chemistry. Again, the sensing function belongs to Met30 within a Skp1-containing SCF—not to Skp1 itself. (johnson2024evidencefora pages 1-2, johnson2024evidencefora pages 6-8)

These 2024 results illustrate a current expert view of SCF biology: F-box proteins can be regulated environmental sensors as well as substrate receptors, while Skp1 supplies the conserved interface through which their association with the catalytic core is assembled or dismantled.

9. Research applications and real-world relevance

  1. Cell-cycle and targeted-proteolysis research. Yeast Skp1 is a foundational model for understanding modular cullin–RING ligases, phosphodegron-dependent substrate selection, and proteasomal control of CDK transitions. The direct value is mechanistic rather than clinical: manipulating Skp1 generally perturbs many SCFs and is less selective than manipulating a particular F-box receptor. (kitagawa1999sgt1encodesan pages 1-2, harris2024molecularinsightsintoa pages 24-27)

  2. Kinetochore assembly and chromosome segregation. The genetically compact budding-yeast point centromere makes Skp1–Ctf13–Cep3 an experimentally tractable model for coupling sequence-specific centromere recognition to kinetochore assembly. The 3.6-Å CBF3 structure provides a framework for testing interface mutations and chromosome-segregation defects. (leber2018structuralbasisfor pages 1-2, leber2018structuralbasisfor pages 5-6)

  3. Chaperone-assisted complex biogenesis. Quantitative Sgt1–Skp1 binding and structural data make this system useful for studying how Hsp90/cochaperones assemble multiprotein machines without remaining permanent subunits. (willhoft2017thecrystalstructure pages 2-3, kitagawa1999sgt1encodesan pages 5-6)

  4. Environmental and nutrient sensing. The 2024 SCF^Met30 studies connect a Skp1-based ligase to cadmium detoxification, glutathione homeostasis, sulfur flux, and H₂S signaling. Potential biotechnology relevance includes understanding yeast robustness under metal or nutrient stress, but no direct industrial SKP1 engineering implementation was established by the retrieved evidence. (lauinger2024cadmiumbindingby pages 8-9, johnson2024evidencefora pages 1-2)

  5. Membrane-trafficking models. The Rcy1–Skp1 complex demonstrates that Skp1–F-box modules can be repurposed outside canonical cullin E3 ligases and supports mechanistic dissection of post-endocytic SNARE recycling. (galan2001skp1pandthe pages 5-7, galan2001skp1pandthe pages 10-11)

10. Evidence-weighted conclusion

The most defensible primary annotation is: Skp1 is an essential, conserved F-box-binding adaptor that organizes multiple protein complexes. Its two best-established essential contexts are canonical SCF ubiquitin ligases and the CBF3 inner kinetochore. In SCFs it couples receptor-mediated substrate recognition to Cdc53–Rbx1/E2-dependent ubiquitylation; in CBF3 it binds Ctf13 and Cep3 to assemble the centromere-recognition apparatus. Additional direct evidence supports transient Sgt1 association and a noncanonical Rcy1-dependent function in Snc1 recycling. (kitagawa1999sgt1encodesan pages 1-2, kitagawa1999sgt1encodesan pages 5-6, leber2018structuralbasisfor pages 5-6, galan2001skp1pandthe pages 1-1)

The annotation should avoid three common errors: calling Skp1 the catalytic E3 enzyme, assigning it direct substrate specificity, or describing it as the direct cadmium/H₂S sensor. Catalysis resides in the assembled RING/E2 machinery, substrate recognition ordinarily resides in the F-box receptor, and the recent stress-sensing chemistry maps to Met30. (harris2024molecularinsightsintoa pages 24-27, lauinger2024cadmiumbindingby pages 1-2, johnson2024evidencefora pages 6-8)

📚 Additional Documentation

Notes

(SKP1-notes.md)

SKP1 (yeast, P52286 / YDR328C / CBF3D) - curation notes

2026-09-26 - full review of the seeded GOA rows

Inputs: SKP1-uniprot.txt, SKP1-goa.tsv (174 rows, 101 of them GO:0005515 IPI from IntAct),
SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md (Edison/Falcon; covers SCF, CBF3, Sgt1-Hsp90 and Rcy1 but not RAVE),
cached publications for all 44 cited PMIDs (full text for 17 of them; the rest are abstract-only).
Comparators: genes/yeast/CDC4 and genes/yeast/CDC53 (both COMPLETE) and genes/human/SKP1.

Gestalt

Skp1 is a non-catalytic adaptor whose one molecular trick is binding F-box motifs while its
N-terminal BTB/POZ-like region binds a cullin (or, in CBF3, contacts Cep3). Everything in GOA
follows from which partner it is holding.

  1. SCF adaptor. Cloned as a cdc4 suppressor; defined the F-box
    PMID:8706131.
    Required for Sic1/Cln/Clb5 proteolysis
    PMID:8706131.
    Bridges Cdc53 to receptors
    PMID:9499404;
    the Met30 F-box is necessary and sufficient
    PMID:9499404,
    confirmed by mapping to residues 180-225
    PMID:14660673.
    Reconstituted SCF(Cdc4) ubiquitinates phospho-Sic1
    PMID:9346239,
    and thirteen SCFs were built on Skp1/Cdc53
    PMID:14747994.
    Allele map used throughout: skp1-11 (G160E/R167K) loses F-box binding, skp1-12 (L8G) loses Cdc53 binding
    PMID:19942853.
    Phospho-S162 weakens Met30 binding
    PMID:22817900.
  2. CBF3 subunit (Cbf3d). Fourth subunit, equal stoichiometry with Ctf13
    PMID:8706132;
    identified independently by reconstitution
    PMID:8670864.
    Skp1-Ctf13 heterodimer
    PMID:10352012.
    Activation needs Hsp90, not phosphorylation
    PMID:12084919;
    Skp1-Sgt1 acts at the rate-limiting step
    PMID:15090617.
    skp1-4 has missegregation and a 2C/short-spindle arrest
    PMID:8706132;
    skp1-3 arrests in G1
    PMID:8706132.
  3. RAVE subunit. Rav1-Rav2-Skp1
    PMID:11283612;
    essential for V-ATPase assembly, with Skp1 binding constitutive
    PMID:11844802.
  4. Localisation. Nucleus + cytoplasm by functional GFP
    PMID:11080155;
    mostly cytoplasmic on fractionation
    PMID:10352012;
    at origins by ChIP as SCF(Dia2)
    PMID:16421250.
  5. Neddylation. Rub1-Cdc53 absent in skp1 alleles
    PMID:9531531;
    explained later by Lag2 eviction
    PMID:19942853.

Decisions and why

Action counts: ACCEPT 41, MODIFY 42, REMOVE 70, KEEP_AS_NON_CORE 16, MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED 5. No PENDING.

  • Protein binding (101 rows). Policy from the annotation-reviewer skill: MODIFY where the cited
    paper supports a specific MF, otherwise REMOVE as uninformative.
  • F-box proteins in focused SCF/CBF3 papers (Bai 1996, Patton 1998, Rouillon 2000, Brunson 2004,
    Kus 2004, Seol 2001, Rodrigo-Brenni 2004, Beltrao 2012, Hwang 2006) -> MODIFY to GO:1990444
    F-box domain binding (26 rows). For Hwang 2006 (abstract does not mention Skp1) the F-box
    binding of Hrt3/Ucc1 is supported by their reconstitution in Kus 2004, cited as additional reference.
  • Cdc53 in focused papers (Patton 1998, Seol 2001, Kus 2004, Siergiejuk 2009) -> MODIFY to
    GO:0097602 cullin family protein binding + GO:0160072 ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity
    (mirrors the human SKP1 review and the human SCF GO-CAMs).
  • HTP/incidental records (Uetz, Ito, Ho, Gavin, Yu, Kato, Breitkreutz, Hazbun, Meier, Michaelis,
    Weerasekera, Thelander, Ang) -> REMOVE (66 rows), same grading as the CDC4 exemplar used for the
    identical references. Eft2, Rav1, Sgt1 rows -> REMOVE (no MF term describes Skp1's side; RAVE and
    kinetochore-assembly rows carry the biology).
  • Bub1 (Kitagawa 2003) -> MODIFY to GO:0007094 mitotic spindle assembly checkpoint signaling,
    because the paper's claim is functional
    PMID:12769845;
    flagged in suggested_questions since SGD did not add a checkpoint term.
  • G2/M transition (3 rows) -> KEEP_AS_NON_CORE, matching CDC4/CDC53: a 2C short-spindle arrest
    is a metaphase-like block of undefined mechanism (kinetochore vs Sic1-independent SCF).
  • Vacuolar acidification (3) and regulation of complex assembly (2) -> MODIFY to GO:0070072:
    RAVE performs assembly, acidification is the downstream outcome; the assembly term already exists.
    RAVE complex (4) and V-ATPase assembly IDA -> KEEP_AS_NON_CORE (fungal-specific, Skp1 contribution undefined).
  • Protein neddylation (2) -> MODIFY to GO:2000436 positive regulation: Skp1 is required
    permissively (evicts Lag2) but the E1/E2/Dcn1 do the chemistry.
  • DNA replication origin binding -> MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED (same as CDC53): ChIP records SCF(Dia2)
    location, not a binding activity; Dia2 is the origin-binding subunit
    PMID:16421250.
  • Chromosome, telomeric region IEA -> REMOVE: inter-ontology propagation from a NAS process row; no
    Skp1 evidence at telomeres.
  • Intra-S checkpoint NAS -> MODIFY to GO:1904290 (direction inverted; Dia2 mediates recovery
    PMID:23172854).
  • Regulation of mitotic cell cycle NAS -> MODIFY to GO:0000082; protein-containing complex assembly
    IDA -> MODIFY to GO:0051382 (generic parents of already-annotated specific terms).
  • Receptor-specific SCF outputs (GAL1/Mig2, mitochondrial fusion, Sir4 silencing x2, endomembrane) ->
    KEEP_AS_NON_CORE; glucose transport, methylmercury, exit from mitosis (direct), Rok1 translation ->
    MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED. Mitotic-exit regulation (Bfa1) x2 -> KEEP_AS_NON_CORE (single abstract-only study).
  • IBA rows (nucleus, cytoplasm, SCF-dependent catabolism, cullin binding, mitotic cell cycle) all ACCEPT;
    the target's own SGD entry among the WITH sources is expected, not circular.

Core functions written

  1. SCF scaffold: MF GO:0160072 (contributes_to GO:0061630); BP GO:0031146, GO:0016567, GO:0000082;
    nucleus + cytoplasm; in_complex GO:0019005.
  2. CBF3 subunit: MF GO:1990444 F-box domain binding (Ctf13); BP GO:0051382; kinetochore + nucleus;
    in_complex GO:0031518.

RAVE and the Rcy1 complex are deliberately not core functions (see above); they are described in
description and raised in suggested_questions.

Not in GOA but worth knowing (from the deep research; primary papers not cached)

  • Cryo-EM of Cep3(2)-Ctf13-Skp1 at 3.6 A (Leber 2018): Skp1 helices alpha6-alpha8 bind the Ctf13
    F-box, residues 105-112 contact the LRRs, and Y139/N140 substitutions abolish complex formation.
  • Sgt1 TPR-Skp1 BTB crystal structure at 2.8 A (Willhoft 2017), Kd ~0.6-0.7 uM; ~2% of Skp1 is Sgt1-bound.
  • Rcy1-Skp1 complex lacks Cdc53/Hrt1 and is needed for Snc1 recycling (Galan 2001).
  • 2024 SCF(Met30) work: cadmium and H2S sensing reside in Met30, not Skp1; Cdc48 extracts Met30 from the
    Cdc53-Skp1 core.

Open items

  • Whether the skp1-4/skp1-12 mitotic arrest is checkpoint-dependent (experiment suggested).
  • Whether Skp1 phosphorylation (S162, T177) tunes receptor loading in vivo (experiment suggested).
  • The Bub1 checkpoint claim rests on one abstract-only paper.

2026-09-29 - IBA propagation rereview

Rechecked the five IBA rows against the IBA project rubric and the cached support for their target-side
biology:

  • GO:0000278 mitotic cell cycle from PANTHER:PTN000877296 remains broad but sound; the direct
    Bai 1996 yeast abstract establishes the mixed G1/G2 skp1 arrest and the target's own SGD row in
    WITH/FROM is expected, not circular.
  • GO:0005634 nucleus, GO:0005737 cytoplasm, GO:0031146 SCF-dependent proteasomal ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolic process, and GO:0097602 cullin family protein binding from PANTHER:PTN000126179
    remain core Skp1 calls, backed by the Mathias/Koepp/Kaplan localization, SCF receptor, and Cdc53-binding
    papers that were already cached.

genes/yeast/SKP1/SKP1-goa.tsv still names the two PTNs, but the local PAINT snapshot under
interpro/panther/PTHR11165/ currently contains only PTHR11165-metadata.yaml and
PTHR11165-entries.csv, so the review now records each PTN source as SOURCE_STALE_OR_MISSING
while keeping the accepted biological decisions.

Fresh PubMed searches for 2025-2026 Skp1/SKP1/Cbf3d with exact Saccharomyces cerevisiae or
yeast SCF/RAVE terms recovered only a mammalian Rabconnectin-3/V-ATPase paper that mentions yeast
Skp1/RAVE as background; no newer budding-yeast SKP1 paper changes the 2026-09-26 curation.

id: P52286
gene_symbol: SKP1
product_type: PROTEIN

taxon:
  id: NCBITaxon:559292
  label: Saccharomyces cerevisiae
description: 'Skp1 (Cbf3d) is the small, essential adaptor protein of Saccharomyces cerevisiae that couples
  F-box proteins to larger assemblies. Its N-terminal BTB/POZ-like domain binds the N-terminal repeat
  of the cullin Cdc53 and its C-terminal helices clamp the ~40-residue F-box motif, so that in SCF (Skp1-Cdc53-F-box-Hrt1)
  ubiquitin ligases Skp1 holds an interchangeable substrate receptor (Cdc4, Grr1, Met30, Dia2, Mdm30,
  Das1, Saf1, Ufo1, Hrt3 and others) in register with the Hrt1-bound E2 Cdc34. Skp1 has no catalytic activity
  and does not itself recognise substrates; the receptor supplies specificity and the Cdc53-Hrt1 module
  supplies the ubiquitin-transfer chemistry. Through SCF(Cdc4) and SCF(Grr1) Skp1 is required for destruction
  of the Clb-Cdk inhibitor Sic1 and of the G1 cyclins at Start, and skp1 alleles arrest in G1 with stabilised
  Sic1; through other receptors it participates in Met4-dependent sulfur-amino-acid control, Fzo1 turnover
  during mitochondrial fusion, Mig2 and Gal80 degradation in galactose induction, Sir4 ubiquitylation
  at silent chromatin and Mrc1 turnover during S-phase checkpoint recovery. Skp1 binding to Cdc53 also
  displaces the Cand1-like inhibitor Lag2, which is a prerequisite for cullin rubylation (neddylation).
  Independently of ubiquitination, Skp1 is the fourth subunit of the CBF3 centromere-binding complex (Ndc10-Cep3-Ctf13-Skp1):
  it heterodimerises with the F-box/LRR protein Ctf13, and the Ctf13/Skp1 pair must be activated by the
  Sgt1-Hsp90 chaperone system before it can join Cep3 and Ndc10 on the CDEIII element to nucleate kinetochore
  assembly; skp1 alleles that disturb this cycle missegregate chromosomes, arrest in mitosis with short
  spindles and disorganise septins. Skp1 is also a stoichiometric subunit of the RAVE complex (Rav1-Rav2-Skp1)
  that promotes V-ATPase V1-V0 assembly, and forms a cullin-free complex with the F-box protein Rcy1 that
  supports recycling of the v-SNARE Snc1. The protein is distributed between nucleus and cytoplasm, with
  a centromere-bound CBF3 pool, and is highly conserved across eukaryotes (ortholog of human SKP1).'

      Hieter''s skp1-3 allele arrests as multiply budded cells with a G1 DNA content, the classic cdc4/cdc34/cdc53

- term:

  original_reference_id: PMID:14747994
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: Skp1 is required for the G1/S transition as the adaptor of SCF(Cdc4) and SCF(Grr1), the ligases
      that destroy the Clb-Cdk inhibitor Sic1 and the G1 cyclins; skp1 alleles arrest in G1 with unreplicated
      DNA and stabilised Sic1.

      (Cdc4 or Grr1) on the Cdc53-Hrt1 core so that phosphorylated Sic1 or Cln1/2 can be ubiquitinated,
      and the reconstituted SCF(Cdc4) and SCF(Grr1) complexes require it. The same term is accepted for
      Cdc4 and Cdc53 in this repository and Skp1 is the yeast exemplar in the G1/S module. The author
      statement accompanies a reconstitution in which purified SCF(Cdc4), built on Skp1, ubiquitinates
      Sic1 with Cdc34 (and Ubc4).'

        catalyzed by two of the five E2 enzymes tested in vitro; Cdc34 and Ubc4
- term:
    id: GO:0000086
    label: G2/M transition of mitotic cell cycle
  evidence_type: IMP
  original_reference_id: PMID:8706131
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: Certain skp1 alleles (skp1-4, skp1-12) arrest as large-budded cells with 2C DNA and a short
      spindle; the block is genuine but mechanistically undefined (kinetochore/CBF3 failure with checkpoint
      arrest versus a Sic1-independent SCF requirement).
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: Kept as non-core, matching the grading of the same term on Cdc4 and Cdc53. The arrest is reproducible
      and is the phenotype that first linked Skp1 to the kinetochore, but a short-spindle, 2C arrest is
      a metaphase-like block rather than a demonstrated defect in the G2/M transition itself, and no substrate
      or CBF3 step has been assigned to it. The evidence supports a second role of Skp1 rather than its
      defining function. Bai et al. report that different skp1 alleles arrest in G1 or in G2.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:8706131
      supporting_text: Different skp1 mutants arrest cells in either G1 or G2, suggesting a connection
        between regulation of proteolysis in different stages of the cycle.

    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: The SCF does the work of this regulatory step (ubiquitinating Mig2 so that it vacates the

- term:
    id: GO:0000921
    label: septin ring assembly
  evidence_type: IMP
  original_reference_id: PMID:16330709
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: skp1-3 and skp1-4, alleles that perturb the CBF3 assembly/turnover cycle through the Skp1-Sgt1
      interaction, cause disorganised septins, random bud-scar patterns and cytokinesis failures.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: 'Genuine mutant phenotype (full text cached) but a secondary, CBF3-dependent role: the authors
      propose that CBF3 acts as a passenger-like complex with Bir1 to coordinate segregation with cytokinesis,
      and only alleles affecting the CBF3 cycle, not outer-kinetochore mutants, affect septins. Skp1 contributes
      by assembling CBF3 rather than by organising septins itself, so the term is kept as a pleiotropic
      non-core process.'
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:16330709
      supporting_text: Specifically, the skp1-4 allele, which prevents CBF3 assembly by blocking the interaction
        between Skp1p and Sgt1p, gives rise to defects in septin organization.
    - reference_id: PMID:16330709
      supporting_text: Only mutations that affect the CBF3 cycle, and not mutants in outer kinetochore
        subunits, cause defects in septins.
- term:
    id: GO:0003688
    label: DNA replication origin binding
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:16421250
  qualifier: enables
  review:
    summary: Skp1 (with Cdc53 and Dia2) co-precipitates ARS305 and ARS603 origin DNA in crosslinker-dependent
      ChIP, reflecting recruitment of SCF(Dia2) to origins.
    action: MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED
    reason: 'The ChIP result is genuine (full text cached) but records the location of an SCF(Dia2) pool,
      not a binding activity of Skp1: Skp1 has no DNA-binding domain, the authors conclude that Dia2 is
      the origin-binding protein, and Skp1 reaches origins only as the F-box adaptor of that complex.
      A molecular-function annotation to origin DNA over-reads crosslinked co-precipitation; this matches
      the grading of the same row on Cdc53. A chromatin/origin location on the SCF(Dia2) complex would
      represent the finding better.'
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:16421250
      supporting_text: both Skp1 and Cdc53 coprecipitated with ARS305 and ARS603 DNA in a cross-linker
        dependent manner
    - reference_id: PMID:16421250
      supporting_text: We propose that Dia2 is an origin-binding protein that plays a role in regulating
        DNA replication.
- term:

  evidence_type: IDA

  qualifier: contributes_to
  review:
    summary: 'Skp1 contributes to the ubiquitin transferase (E3) activity of reconstituted SCF(Cdc4):

- term:
    id: GO:0005515
    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:10637232
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:P39014
  review:
    summary: Met30 is an F-box protein; the informative activity behind this interaction is Skp1 binding
      the F-box motif of Met30, which is how Skp1 tethers the receptor to the Cdc53-Hrt1 core (or, for
      Ctf13, into CBF3).
    action: MODIFY
    reason: 'The cited work supports a more informative molecular function than bare protein binding:
      F-box domain binding (GO:1990444). Skp1 binds F-box proteins through the ~40-residue F-box motif
      (Bai et al., PMID:8706131), and this is the defining contact of the adaptor. Rouillon et al. (full
      text cached) show the Skp1p-Met30p association is F-box-dependent and constitutive with respect
      to methionine.'
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:1990444
      label: F-box domain binding
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:10637232
      supporting_text: Met30p was shown to associate with Skp1p and Cdc53p in an F-box-dependent manner
    - reference_id: PMID:10637232
      supporting_text: Immunoprecipitation of HA-Met30 followed by immunoblotting with polyclonal antibodies
        directed against Skp1p revealed that the specific Skp1p–Met30p interaction is neither increased
        nor decreased by the presence of high extracellular methionine concentrations

  - UniProtKB:P38352
  review:
    summary: Saf1 is an F-box protein; the informative activity behind this interaction is Skp1 binding
      the F-box motif of Saf1, which is how Skp1 tethers the receptor to the Cdc53-Hrt1 core (or, for
      Ctf13, into CBF3).
    action: MODIFY
    reason: 'The cited work supports a more informative molecular function than bare protein binding:
      F-box domain binding (GO:1990444). Skp1 binds F-box proteins through the ~40-residue F-box motif
      (Bai et al., PMID:8706131), and this is the defining contact of the adaptor. Seol et al. recovered
      Saf1 among the nine F-box proteins associated with Skp1 by sequential affinity purification and
      mass spectrometry; the interaction is through the F-box, as for every other receptor.'
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:1990444
      label: F-box domain binding

      supporting_text: 16 Skp1 and Cdc53-associated proteins in budding yeast, including all components

  review:
    summary: Cdc53 is the cullin scaffold of SCF; the informative activity behind this interaction is
      Skp1 binding the N-terminal cullin repeat of Cdc53, the second of the two contacts that define the
      adaptor.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: The cited work supports the specific molecular function cullin family protein binding (GO:0097602),
      the term already carried by IBA and used for the human SKP1-CUL1 rows, rather than bare protein
      binding; because the cullin contact is one half of the bridge by which Skp1 joins the receptor to
      the Cdc53-Hrt1 core, the activity it enables is ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity (GO:0160072),
      the term used for human SKP1 in the SCF GO-CAM models. Seol et al. recovered Cdc53 and all SCF components
      in sequential Skp1/Cdc53 purifications.
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0097602
      label: cullin family protein binding
    - id: GO:0160072
      label: ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:11283612
      supporting_text: 16 Skp1 and Cdc53-associated proteins in budding yeast, including all components
        of SCF, 9 FBPs, Yjr033 (Rav1) and Ydr202 (Rav2)
    - reference_id: PMID:11283612
      supporting_text: SCF ubiquitin ligases are composed of Skp1, Cdc53, Hrt1 and one member of a large
        family of substrate receptors known as F-box proteins (FBPs).

- term:
    id: GO:0005515
    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:12769845
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - SGD:S000003420
  review:
    summary: Bub1 associates with centromere DNA via Skp1, and a Skp1 mutant that cannot bind Bub1 fails
      to mount the mitotic delay triggered by kinetochore tension defects while retaining the nocodazole,
      kinetochore-assembly and Mps1-overexpression arrests.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: Bare protein binding hides the functional claim of the paper, which is that the Skp1-Bub1
      contact transmits the tension-defect signal into the spindle checkpoint. The better term is mitotic
      spindle assembly checkpoint signaling (GO:0007094), which the authors support with a separation-of-function
      Skp1 allele. This is a single, abstract-only study on a role separate from SCF and CBF3 assembly,
      so the replacement should be treated as non-core; SGD did not add a checkpoint process term from
      this paper, and the proposal is flagged in suggested_questions.
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0007094
      label: mitotic spindle assembly checkpoint signaling
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:12769845
      supporting_text: The Skp1's interaction with Bub1 is required for the mitotic delay induced by kinetochore
        tension defects, but not for the arrest induced by spindle depolymerization, kinetochore assembly
        defects, or Mps1 overexpression.
    - reference_id: PMID:12769845
      supporting_text: We propose that the Skp1-Bub1 interaction is important for transmitting a signal
        to the spindle checkpoint pathway when insufficient tension is present at kinetochores.

      the Skp1-Sgt1 contact (Sgt1 supplies the TPR domain; Skp1 is the ligand). Bare protein binding adds
      no functional information about Skp1, so the row is removed; removal does not mean the interaction

    reason: 'The cited work supports a more informative molecular function than bare protein binding:
      F-box domain binding (GO:1990444). Skp1 binds F-box proteins through the ~40-residue F-box motif
      (Bai et al., PMID:8706131), and this is the defining contact of the adaptor. The cached abstract
      does not describe the Skp1 assay, but Ucc1 (Ylr224w) is an F-box protein and its SCF assembly with
      Skp1 is shown independently by reconstitution (Kus et al., PMID:14747994), so the informative term
      is F-box domain binding.'
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:1990444
      label: F-box domain binding
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:17141224
      supporting_text: We found that overexpression of Hrt3 and of Ylr224w rendered yeast cells resistant
        to methylmercury.

    - PMID:14747994

  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q12018
  review:
    summary: Cdc53 is the cullin scaffold of SCF; the informative activity behind this interaction is
      Skp1 binding the N-terminal cullin repeat of Cdc53, the second of the two contacts that define the
      adaptor.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: 'The cited work supports the specific molecular function cullin family protein binding (GO:0097602),
      the term already carried by IBA and used for the human SKP1-CUL1 rows, rather than bare protein
      binding; because the cullin contact is one half of the bridge by which Skp1 joins the receptor to
      the Cdc53-Hrt1 core, the activity it enables is ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity (GO:0160072),
      the term used for human SKP1 in the SCF GO-CAM models. Full text cached: Cdc53 is in Skp1 immunoprecipitates,
      the skp1-12 L8G mutation abolishes Cdc53 binding, and Skp1 binding to Cdc53 is what evicts the Cand1-like
      inhibitor Lag2.'
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0097602
      label: cullin family protein binding
    - id: GO:0160072
      label: ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:19942853
      supporting_text: Conversely, Cdc53 but not Lag2 was found in Skp1 immunoprecipitates
    - reference_id: PMID:19942853
      supporting_text: skp1-12 carries a single mutation (L8G) that disrupts binding to Cdc53

- term:
    id: GO:0007035
    label: vacuolar acidification
  evidence_type: IGI
  original_reference_id: PMID:11283612
  qualifier: involved_in
  supporting_entities:
  - SGD:S000002610
  review:
    summary: Skp1 is a subunit of the RAVE complex (Rav1-Rav2-Skp1), which binds cytosolic V1 sectors
      and promotes assembly of the V-ATPase holoenzyme; loss of RAVE gives the vma phenotype. Genetic
      interaction row with RAV1.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: 'The term names the downstream outcome (proton pumping by the assembled V-ATPase) rather than
      the step RAVE performs. RAVE is an assembly factor: it associates with V1 released by glucose deprivation
      and is needed for stable V1-V0 assembly even in glucose-grown cells, so the process Skp1 participates
      in is V-ATPase complex assembly (GO:0070072), already annotated from Smardon et al. Proposing that
      term as the replacement keeps the evidence and drops the indirect claim. Skp1''s own contribution
      inside RAVE remains undefined (its recruitment is constitutive and is not the assembly signal),
      so the RAVE function is graded non-core.'
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0070072
      label: vacuolar proton-transporting V-type ATPase complex assembly
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:11283612
      supporting_text: here we show that RAVE promotes glucose-triggered assembly of the V-ATPase holoenzyme
    - reference_id: PMID:11844802
      supporting_text: but also demonstrate an essential role in V-ATPase assembly under other conditions

- term:
    id: GO:0007096
    label: regulation of exit from mitosis
  evidence_type: IMP
  original_reference_id: PMID:17205042
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: skp1-12 (an allele defective for Cdc53 binding) shows mitotic-exit and cytokinesis defects
      and a specific genetic interaction with bfa1-delta; Skp1 binds the C-terminal 184 residues of the
      MEN inhibitor Bfa1 without affecting Bfa1 turnover.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: Single abstract-only study (J Microbiol 2006) proposing an SCF-independent role in mitotic
      exit; the phenotype and the Bfa1 interaction are reported directly, but no mechanism (Skp1 does
      not control Bfa1 abundance) and no independent confirmation exist, and skp1-12 also perturbs CBF3-dependent
      functions that could delay exit indirectly. Kept as a non-core, provisional role rather than removed.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:17205042
      supporting_text: we found that the skp1-12 mutant allele, previously reported to block G2-M transition,
        showed defects in mitotic exit and cytokinesis
    - reference_id: PMID:17205042
      supporting_text: We suggest a novel function of Skp1 in mitotic exit and cytokinesis, independent
        of its function as a part of the SCF complex.

  review:
    summary: Skp1 (Cbf3d) is the fourth subunit of CBF3 (Ndc10/Cbf2, Cep3, Ctf13, Skp1), the complex that
      binds centromeric CDEIII DNA; it heterodimerises with the F-box protein Ctf13 and is required for

      the yeast SKP1 homologue.

        named Cbf3d.

- term:
    id: GO:0031573
    label: mitotic intra-S DNA damage checkpoint signaling
  evidence_type: NAS
  original_reference_id: PMID:23172854
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: 'ComplexPortal row for SCF(Dia2): Dia2 is needed for robust Rad53 deactivation and Mrc1 degradation
      during recovery from MMS damage, i.e. for switching the S-phase checkpoint off.'
    action: MODIFY
    reason: 'The direction of the term is wrong: the paper shows SCF(Dia2) mediates checkpoint recovery
      (Rad53 deactivation, Mrc1 turnover), not checkpoint signalling. The matching concept is negative
      regulation of mitotic DNA damage checkpoint (GO:1904290), as proposed for the same row on Cdc53;
      for the adaptor this remains a receptor-specific, non-core output.'
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:1904290
      label: negative regulation of mitotic DNA damage checkpoint
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:23172854
      supporting_text: Dia2 is required for robust deactivation of the Rad53 checkpoint kinase and timely
        completion of DNA replication during recovery from DNA damage induced by methyl methanesulfonate
        (MMS).
    - reference_id: PMID:23172854
      supporting_text: Dia2 contributes to Mrc1 degradation during S-phase checkpoint recovery

  review:
    summary: Skp1 is a subunit of the RAVE complex (Rav1-Rav2-Skp1), which binds cytosolic V1 sectors
      and promotes assembly of the V-ATPase holoenzyme; loss of RAVE gives the vma phenotype. Physical-interaction
      row with RAV1.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: 'Too general: the complex whose assembly RAVE promotes is the V-ATPase, and the same paper
      (and Smardon et al.) shows RAVE is an assembly factor for it, so the specific term GO:0070072, already
      annotated by IDA, is the right one. The RAVE role is a secondary, yeast-specific Skp1 function.'
    proposed_replacement_terms:

    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:11283612

    id: GO:0043291
    label: RAVE complex
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:11283612
  qualifier: part_of
  review:
    summary: Skp1 is a stoichiometric subunit of the RAVE complex (Rav1-Rav2-Skp1), which associates with
      cytosolic V1 sectors and is required for stable V-ATPase assembly. ComplexPortal row.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: Well-established complex membership (RAVE is defined in GO as Rav1p-Rav2p-Skp1p) from sequential
      affinity purification and mass spectrometry, confirmed by Smardon et al. It is a non-SCF, fungal-specific
      assembly in which Skp1's molecular contribution is undefined (its binding is constitutive and not
      the assembly signal), so it is kept as a genuine non-core component rather than a core function.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:11283612
      supporting_text: Rav1, Rav2 and Skp1 form a complex that we have named 'regulator of the (H+)-ATPase
        of the vacuolar and endosomal membranes' (RAVE)

- term:
    id: GO:0045116
    label: protein neddylation
  evidence_type: IGI
  original_reference_id: PMID:9531531
  qualifier: involved_in
  supporting_entities:
  - SGD:S000005924
  review:
    summary: Rub1 (Nedd8) conjugation to Cdc53 is absent in skp1-3, skp1-4 and skp1-12 cells and restored
      by SKP1; later work showed Skp1 binding to Cdc53 evicts the Cand1-like inhibitor Lag2, a prerequisite
      for cullin neddylation. Genetic-interaction row with ENR2 (ULA1).
    action: MODIFY
    reason: 'Skp1 is required for, but does not perform, Rub1 conjugation: the Rub1 E1 (Enr2/Ula1-Uba3),
      E2 (Ubc12) and the Dcn1-dependent ligase do the chemistry, and Siergiejuk et al. (full text cached)
      show that the Skp1 requirement is explained by displacement of Lag2 from the Skp1-binding pocket
      of Cdc53, so that skp1-12 (defective in Cdc53 binding) loses neddylation and lag2-delta restores
      it. A positive-regulation term captures that permissive role; the direct process term over-states
      it. Proposed replacement: positive regulation of protein neddylation (GO:2000436).'
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:2000436
      label: positive regulation of protein neddylation
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:19942853
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:9531531
      supporting_text: Second, we observe a strong enhancement of both the skp1-11 and skp1-12 phenotype
        in enr2Δ double mutants, strongly suggesting the involvement of ENR2 and SKP1 in common functions.
    - reference_id: PMID:19942853
      supporting_text: On the basis of these results we conclude that Skp1 is required to trigger Lag2
        dissociation from cullins in vivo , which is a prerequisite for subsequent cullin neddylation.

- term:
    id: GO:0051382
    label: kinetochore assembly
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:12084919
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: 'Skp1 nucleates kinetochore assembly as the partner of Ctf13: the Ctf13p/Skp1p heterodimer
      must be activated by Hsp90 (and Sgt1) to bind Cep3 and Ndc10 on CDEIII, and the Skp1p-Sgt1p interaction
      contributes to the rate-limiting binding of Ctf13p to Ndc10p.'
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: 'Core biological process. Skp1 does part of the work: it binds and stabilises the Ctf13 F-box/LRR
      core, and Skp1-Sgt1-Hsp90 action converts Ctf13/Skp1 into the CEN-binding-competent form that seeds
      CBF3 and hence the entire kinetochore. Stemmann et al. (full text cached) show Hsp90 is required
      to form active Ctf13p/Skp1p and that phosphorylation of either subunit is dispensable.'
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:12084919
      supporting_text: Binding of CBF3, a protein complex consisting of Ndc10p, Cep3p, Ctf13p, and Skp1p,
        to the centromere DNA nucleates kinetochore formation in budding yeast.
    - reference_id: PMID:12084919
      supporting_text: Instead, the formation of active Ctf13p/Skp1p requires Hsp90.

    reason: 'Core molecular function with the correct contributes_to qualifier: Skp1, Cdc53 and Cdc4 form
      the Sic1 E3, Cdc4 assembled with Skp1 is the phospho-Sic1 receptor, and Skp1 itself catalyses nothing.
      Skp1''s own activity is best described as ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity (GO:0160072).'
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:9346238
      supporting_text: Skp1, Cdc53, and the F-box protein Cdc4 form a complex, SCFCdc4, which functions
        as a Sic1 ubiquitin-ligase (E3) in combination with the ubiquitin conjugating enzyme (E2) Cdc34
        and E1.
    - reference_id: PMID:9346238
      supporting_text: Cdc4 assembled with Skp1 functions as the receptor that selectively binds phosphorylated
        Sic1.
- term:
    id: GO:0065003
    label: protein-containing complex assembly
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:15090617
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: 'SGD row from the CBF3 assembly study: Skp1p and Sgt1p act on Ctf13p in the rate-limiting
      step of CBF3 assembly.'
    action: MODIFY
    reason: Too general. The complex assembled is CBF3, the inner-kinetochore scaffold, and the same paper
      is already the source of the kinetochore assembly (GO:0051382) row; proposing that specific term
      in place of the generic parent removes an uninformative duplicate.
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0051382
      label: kinetochore assembly
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:15090617
      supporting_text: We have found that the interaction between Skp1p and Sgt1p is critical for the
        assembly of CBF3 complexes.
- term:
    id: GO:0070072
    label: vacuolar proton-transporting V-type ATPase complex assembly
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:11844802
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: Skp1 is a stoichiometric subunit of the RAVE complex (Rav1-Rav2-Skp1), which associates with
      cytosolic V1 sectors and is required for stable V-ATPase assembly. RAVE binds V1 reversibly after
      glucose deprivation and constitutively in cells lacking V0, and V-ATPase from RAVE-deficient cells
      is structurally and functionally defective even in glucose.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: The process is the one RAVE actually performs, so it is the correct term for the RAVE-bound
      pool of Skp1 and is the replacement proposed for the vacuolar-acidification rows. It is nevertheless
      a secondary, non-SCF function in which Skp1's specific contribution is unknown (Smardon et al. show
      Skp1 binding to RAVE is constitutive and not the assembly signal), so it is kept as non-core.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:11844802
      supporting_text: Here, we provide evidence supporting a role for RAVE in reassembly of the V-ATPase
        but also demonstrate an essential role in V-ATPase assembly under other conditions.
    - reference_id: PMID:11844802
      supporting_text: Skp1p recruitment to the RAVE complex does not appear to provide a signal for V-ATPase
        assembly

- term:
    id: GO:2000766
    label: negative regulation of cytoplasmic translation
  evidence_type: IMP
  original_reference_id: PMID:26310304
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: Skp1 was recovered as a ROK1 5'UTR-interacting protein in a yeast three-hybrid screen, and
      a skp1 temperature-sensitive allele derepressed Rok1 protein synthesis through uORF1.
    action: MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED
    reason: Single abstract-only study. The IMP rests on shifting a temperature-sensitive skp1 allele,
      which also arrests the cell cycle, while Rok1 expression is itself cell-cycle-regulated (declining
      at G1/S), so the derepression is plausibly an indirect consequence of SCF/CBF3 loss rather than
      a translational activity of Skp1, which has no RNA-binding domain and no other link to translation.
      Not removed, because the assay was done, but over-annotated relative to the evidence.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:26310304
      supporting_text: Rok1 protein expression is cell cycle-regulated, declining at G1/S and increasing
        at G2.
    - reference_id: PMID:26310304
      supporting_text: A deletion analysis of PSK2 or inactivation of temperature-sensitive alleles of
        SKP1 and TUB4 revealed that Rok1 protein synthesis is repressed by Psk2 and Skp1.

- id: file:yeast/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md
  title: Falcon deep research report for yeast SKP1
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Edison/Falcon literature synthesis; its adaptor framing (SCF, CBF3, Sgt1-Hsp90, Rcy1)
      agrees with the cached primary papers and UniProt; it does not cover RAVE.
core_functions:
- description: 'Adaptor/scaffold of SCF (Skp1-Cdc53-F-box-Hrt1) ubiquitin ligases: the BTB/POZ-like N-terminus
    binds the cullin Cdc53 while the C-terminal helices bind the F-box motif of an interchangeable receptor
    (Cdc4, Grr1, Met30, Dia2, Mdm30, Das1, Saf1, Ufo1, Hrt3 and others), holding the receptor-bound phospho-substrate
    in register with the Hrt1-bound E2 Cdc34 so that Sic1, Cln1/2, Met4, Far1 and other targets are polyubiquitinated
    for proteasomal destruction; Sic1 and Cln removal drives the G1/S transition.'
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0160072
    label: ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity
  contributes_to_molecular_function:
    id: GO:0061630
    label: ubiquitin protein ligase activity
  directly_involved_in:
  - id: GO:0031146
    label: SCF-dependent proteasomal ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolic process
  - id: GO:0016567
    label: protein ubiquitination
  - id: GO:0000082
    label: G1/S transition of mitotic cell cycle
  locations:
  - id: GO:0005634
    label: nucleus
  - id: GO:0005737
    label: cytoplasm
  in_complex:
    id: GO:0019005
    label: SCF ubiquitin ligase complex
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: PMID:9499404
    supporting_text: We find that Skp1 interacts with Cdc53 in vivo, and that Skp1 bridges Cdc53 to three
      different F-box proteins, Cdc4, Met30, and Grr1.
  - reference_id: PMID:8706131
    supporting_text: directly binds Skp2p, cyclin F, and Cdc4p through a novel structural motif called
      the F-box
  - reference_id: PMID:9346238
    supporting_text: Skp1, Cdc53, and the F-box protein Cdc4 form a complex, SCFCdc4, which functions
      as a Sic1 ubiquitin-ligase (E3) in combination with the ubiquitin conjugating enzyme (E2) Cdc34
      and E1.
  - reference_id: PMID:9346239
    supporting_text: Phosphorylated Sic1p substrate is specifically targeted for ubiquitination by binding
      to a Cdc4p/Skp1p subcomplex.
  - reference_id: PMID:10213692
    supporting_text: Phosphorylated Cln1 was ubiquitinated by SCF (Skp1-Cdc53-F-box protein) complexes
      containing the F-box protein Grr1, Rbx1, and the E2 Cdc34.
  - reference_id: PMID:11080155
    supporting_text: The core SCF subunits Cdc53, Hrt1 and Skp1 were distributed in the nucleus and the
      cytoplasm, whereas the F-box protein Cdc4 was exclusively nuclear.
  - reference_id: file:yeast/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md
    supporting_text: Skp1 is an essential, nonenzymatic protein-interaction adaptor.
  - reference_id: file:yeast/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md
    supporting_text: In canonical SCF ligases, Skp1 connects an F-box substrate receptor to the Cdc53/Cul1–Rbx1/Hrt1
      catalytic scaffold.
- description: 'F-box-binding subunit of the CBF3 inner-kinetochore complex: Skp1 heterodimerises with
    the F-box/LRR protein Ctf13, and the Ctf13/Skp1 pair, once activated by the Sgt1-Hsp90 chaperone system,
    assembles with the Cep3 and Ndc10 dimers on centromeric CDEIII DNA to nucleate kinetochore formation;
    Skp1-Sgt1 binding contributes to the rate-limiting Ctf13-Ndc10 step and balances CBF3 assembly against
    Ctf13 turnover.'

proposed_new_terms: []
suggested_questions:
- question: What is Skp1's molecular contribution inside the RAVE complex and the cullin-free Rcy1-Skp1
    complex? Rav1 and Rcy1 bind Skp1 through F-box-like contacts, yet neither assembly contains Cdc53/Hrt1;
    does Skp1 act as a structural adaptor there, or does it recruit an alternative partner, and should
    these pools carry a molecular function distinct from ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity?
- question: Should the Skp1-Bub1 tension-checkpoint finding (PMID:12769845), now recorded only as protein
    binding, be represented as a mitotic spindle assembly checkpoint signaling annotation, and is it reproducible
    with the separation-of-function skp1 allele in a clean background given that SGD did not add a checkpoint
    term from the paper?
- question: Which of the receptor-specific downstream outputs attached to the shared adaptor (HXT induction,
    GAL1 derepression, mitochondrial fusion, Sir4-dependent silencing, checkpoint recovery, methylmercury
    resistance) should be modelled as SCF(F-box) complex-level GO-CAM activities with the F-box protein
    as the specificity subunit, leaving Skp1 with the scaffold activity and the SCF-dependent catabolic
    process?
suggested_experiments:
- hypothesis: The G2/M (metaphase-like) arrest of skp1-4 and skp1-12 cells is caused by loss of CBF3-dependent
    kinetochore function and consequent spindle-checkpoint activation, not by a Sic1-independent SCF requirement.
  description: Combine skp1-4 and skp1-12 with mad2-delta or bub1-delta and score spindle length, Pds1
    stability and anaphase entry at the restrictive temperature; a checkpoint-dependent arrest would be
    bypassed (with missegregation), whereas an SCF-dependent block would persist. In parallel, test a
    Skp1 variant carrying the Ctf13-interface substitutions (Y139/N140) in an otherwise SCF-competent
    background.
  experiment_type: genetic epistasis with checkpoint mutants and interface alleles
- hypothesis: Skp1 phosphorylation at S162 (and T177) tunes receptor selection in vivo by weakening particular
    F-box contacts.
  description: Express phospho-null and phospho-mimetic SKP1 alleles at the endogenous locus and quantify
    the F-box protein repertoire co-purifying with Skp1 by SILAC/MS across nutrient conditions, then measure
    Met4, Sic1 and Cln2 half-lives to link altered receptor loading to substrate turnover.
  experiment_type: phosphosite mutagenesis with quantitative interactome proteomics
